item.title: Local cohomology module with infinitely many associated primes over ramified regular local rings of the least possible dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2611.26655v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In \cite{Ma} we have observed the example of local cohomology module with infinitely many associated primes over a 12 dimensional ramified regular local ring. In this paper we construct examples of local cohomology modules with infinitely many associated primes over ramified regular local rings of two different ring dimensions. The result of this paper is very much dependent on the result (\cite{SS}, Theorem 2.6).
item.dc:creator: Rajsekhar Bhattacharyya

item.title: Studies on a Relationship Between Tate Homology and Local Cohomology of Tensor Products of Modules
item.description: arXiv:2611.26812v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the local cohomology of finitely generated modules with respect to specialization-closed subsets over commutative Noetherian rings. Our main result establishes a relationship between the local cohomology of tensor products of modules and Tate homology over Gorenstein rings. We present several consequences of our main result, which are of independent interest. For example, we study various aspects of the cohomological rigidity property of tensor products of modules and generalize results of Huneke-Wiegand in this direction. We determine conditions under which the vanishing of a single local cohomology module of a tensor product implies the vanishing of all lower ones, establish bounds for the depth of tensor products of modules, and obtain criteria for freeness of modules over complete intersection rings. Along the way, we also provide a splitting criterion for vector bundles on smooth complete intersections.
item.dc:creator: Mohsen Asgharzadeh, Olgur Celikbas, Arash Sadeghi

item.title: Persistent Bass and Lyubeznik Numbers of Stanley Reisner Rings
item.description: arXiv:2611.26813v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We define persistent Lyubeznik numbers and persistent Bass numbers of Stanley--Reisner rings along a simplicial filtration. For Lyubeznik numbers we show that the complex of \`Alvarez Montaner and Vahidi computing $\lambda_{p,q}(\kk[\Delta])$ is natural for inclusions of simplicial complexes, so that persistent Lyubeznik numbers are ranks of maps on its cohomology. We give an equivalent costar complex, whose terms are reduced homology groups of links of faces and whose differentials are induced by quotient maps; it requires neither Alexander duals nor free resolutions. For Bass numbers at coordinate primes we prove that the Hochster-type formula is natural for inclusions, which identifies the persistent Bass numbers with the persistent graded Betti numbers of Suwayyid and Wei for filtered links. Both families have finite barcodes and satisfy bottleneck stability. Examples, including two isomers with the same persistent homology, exhibit Lyubeznik bars that persistent homology does not detect.
item.dc:creator: Kaiyue He, Faisal Suwayyid, Guo-Wei Wei

item.title: The Ritt problem is decidable
item.description: arXiv:2611.27008v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give an affirmative solution to the Ritt problem.
item.dc:creator: Jason Fang, James Freitag, Matthew Harrison-Trainor

item.title: Constructing toric diagonal modules with short linear resolutions
item.description: arXiv:2611.27025v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a complete simplicial toric variety $X$, we construct a collection of Cohen--Macaulay modules with linear resolutions where the associated sheaf is the diagonal. Through this work, we see that the resolutions constructed by Favero--Huang from homotopy path algebras and those constructed by Hanlon--Hicks--Lazarev can be viewed as two dual methods to construct resolutions of the diagonal starting from a compatible $\mathbb{Z}^n$-stratification.
item.dc:creator: Jay Yang

item.title: Squarefree powers of simplicial forests
item.description: arXiv:2611.27531v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The highest nonzero squarefree power of an edge ideal always has linear quotients, whereas this property can fail even for the facet ideal of a pure two-dimensional simplicial tree. This raises the question of which combinatorial conditions ensure linear quotients beyond the graph case. We characterize the squarefree powers of facet ideals of pure simplicial forests that have linear quotients, showing that this property is equivalent to having a linear resolution or being linearly related. We also investigate the corresponding question for undirected path ideals of forests. Here the highest nonzero squarefree power always has linear quotients for $3$-path ideals, whereas the analogous assertion fails for $4$-path ideals of trees.
item.dc:creator: Marie Amalore Nambi, Francesco Navarra, Ayesha Asloob Qureshi, Dharm Veer

item.title: Monomial Ideals Of VEW Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.27812v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $D$ be a $k$-edge weighted VEW graph and $I=I(D)$ be its edge ideal. In this paper, we characterize the irredundant irreducible decomposition of edge ideal $I$. Also, we study the Cohen-Macaulay property and Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity of different classes of $k$-edge weighted VEW graphs.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: M. Kumar and D.K. Pradhan, Monomial ideals of VEW graphs, J. Alg. Appl. 2026
item.dc:creator: Manohar Kumar, Dipak Kumar Pradhan

item.title: $n$-absorbing ideals of rings of continuous functions I: minimal primes, common zero sets, and non-$z$ ideals
item.description: arXiv:2611.26977v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $C(X)$ be the ring of real-valued continuous functions on a Tychonoff space $X$, and for an ideal $I$ let $\K(I)$ be the set of common zeros of its members. We show that a proper $z$-ideal of $C(X)$ is $n$-absorbing if and only if it has at most $n$ minimal primes, if and only if it is an intersection of at most $n$ pairwise incomparable primes, if and only if its filter of zero sets is $n$-absorbing; the algebraic part of this equivalence is valid for radical ideals of any commutative ring. We prove that $|\K(I)|\le n$ for every $n$-absorbing ideal $I$ and that this bound is sharp. We further prove that the $z$-closure of every $n$-absorbing ideal is an $n$-absorbing $z$-ideal and has the same common zero set. Finally, every $n$-absorbing ideal of $C(X)$ is a $z$-ideal if and only if $X$ is a $P$-space. Moreover, for every non-unit $f\in C(X)$, the principal ideal $(f)$ is $n$-absorbing if and only if $\Z(f)$ is clopen and $(f)$ has at most $n$ minimal prime ideals.
item.dc:creator: Ali Akbar Estaji

item.title: Chern classes, Poincar\'e polynomials, and Bernstein-Sato polynomials of plane curves
item.description: arXiv:2611.27297v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that the Poincar\'e polynomial of a reduced plane curve $C$ is the Chern polynomial of the dual of the bundle of Jacobian syzygies of $C$. Using the Zeuthen-Segre formula, we prove that its value at $t=-1$ equals the Euler number of the complement of $C$ up to the correction term $\mu(C)-\tau(C)$, so the two numbers coincide if and only if all singularities of $C$ are quasi-homogeneous. As applications, we show that the defect in a combinatorial inequality for free $d$-arrangements is the square of the difference of the exponents, extend the addition technique to arbitrary reduced plane curves, and locate the roots of local Bernstein-Sato polynomials at ordinary singular points.
item.dc:creator: Piotr Pokora

item.title: Classification of strongly $F$-regular and $F$-pure surface singularities with imperfect residue fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.27597v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study strongly $F$-regular and $F$-pure normal surface singularities whose residue fields are not necessarily perfect. We characterize strong $F$-regularity in terms of the weighted dual graph and geometric reducedness of the exceptional components of the minimal resolution, extending Hara's classification over algebraically closed residue fields. We also determine the possible dual graphs of $F$-pure surface singularities and give converse criteria. Notably, the exceptional components of an $F$-pure surface singularity are geometrically reduced unless the singularity is a rational double point.
item.dc:creator: Tatsuro Kawakami, Kenta Sato

item.title: Invariant rings of Frobenius polarization operators and normal cores of subgroups
item.description: arXiv:2611.27752v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For a proper subgroup $H$ of a finite group $G$, we determine the common kernel, or invariant ring, of the Frobenius polarization operators corresponding to the elements of $G\setminus H$. We show that the invariant rings defined by the left and right polarization operators coincide and depend only on the normal core $N=\operatorname{Core}_G(H)$. We construct polynomials $P_\Omega$ indexed by the orbits of the conjugation action of $G$ on $\widehat N$ and prove that they form an algebraically independent generating set for the invariant ring. We also show that inclusion of these invariant rings as subrings of $\mathbb C[\mathbf{x}]$ is equivalent to inclusion of the corresponding normal cores. For an arbitrary subgroup $H$, we give a factorization of the group determinant in terms of these polynomials. This factorization generalizes Frobenius' group determinant theorem and reduces to its factorization when $H=G$. When $G$ is abelian, each $P_\Omega$ is a specialization of the group determinant of the quotient group $G/H$. Finally, we establish a Capelli identity for each $P_\Omega$ and compute the coefficient polynomial obtained by applying a constant-coefficient differential operator to its powers.
item.dc:creator: Naoya Yamaguchi

item.title: Relative Gr\"obner bases of modules and applications in persistence theory
item.description: arXiv:2603.27149v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Finitely generated modules over the polynomial ring in $n$ indeterminates are isomorphic to quotients of finite rank free modules. We introduce a theory of relative Gr\"obner bases for those quotients of free modules and, equivalently, for pairs of submodules; we prove corresponding Buchberger- and Schreyer-type theorems. As applications of this theory, we consider three problems in persistence theory, which can be solved by relative Gr\"obner bases. First, we show that the relative Schreyer's theorem can be used to compute free presentations of complexes of finitely generated torsion-free modules. In contrast to previous approaches, this allows computation of free presentations for multicritical persistent homology directly at the chain module level without additional topological constructions. Second, any finitely generated Artinian module embeds in an Artinian injective hull, giving rise to a flat-injective presentation. We represent the embedding of the module in this injective hull by a quotient of a free module and apply the relative Schreyer's theorem to construct an algorithm for the computation of a free presentation from a flat-injective presentation. Third, we investigate how free presentations, and more generally free resolutions, obtained by the two preceding applications can be minimized by standard reduction techniques.
item.dc:creator: Fritz Grimpen, Matthias Orth, Anastasios Stefanou

item.title: A DG algebra structure for the edge ideal of any split graph
item.description: arXiv:2610.40540v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct an explicit DG algebra structure on the minimal free resolution of the quotient of a polynomial ring by the edge ideal of any split graph (that is, a graph whose vertex set is a disjoint union of a clique and an independent set). The algebra structure is based on a simple combinatorial notion, which we call the fixing edge of a pair of edges, that directly captures the structure of the underlying graph. Our construction involves an explicit description of the minimal free resolution of the edge ideal of such a graph, including formulas for both the Betti numbers and the differentials.
item.dc:creator: David Bronshvayg, Rachel Diethorn, Mario Stinson-Maas, Reed Wang

item.title: The Baire property and precompact duality
item.description: arXiv:2405.02624v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that if $G$ is a totally bounded abelian group \st\ its dual group $\widehat{G}_p$ equipped with the finite-open topology is a Baire group, then every compact subset of $G$ must be finite. This solves an open question by Chasco, Dom\'inguez and Tkachenko. {Among other consequences, we obtain an example of a group that is $g$-dense in its completion but is not $g$-barrelled. This solves a question proposed by Au${\beta}$enhofer and Dikranjan.}
item.dc:creator: M. Ferrer, S. Hern\'andez, I. Sep\'ulveda, F. J. Trigos-Arrieta

item.title: Lie Algebra Decomposition Classes for Reductive Algebraic Groups in Arbitrary Characteristic
item.description: arXiv:2511.01440v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we investigate the decomposition classes of the Lie algebras of connected reductive algebraic groups, over algebraically closed fields of arbitrary characteristic. We extend some results proved previously under restrictions on the characteristic, including a formula for the dimension of a decomposition class, and introduce Levi-type decomposition classes to account for some of the difficulties encountered in bad characteristic. We also establish properties of Lusztig--Spaltenstein induction of non-nilpotent orbits, such as parabolic independence, extending the known results for nilpotent orbits. Finally, we determine the covering relation for the closure order on decomposition classes, in the case of good characteristic.
item.dc:creator: Joel Summerfield

item.title: Chromatic numbers from edge ideals: Graph classes with vanishing syzygies are polynomially $\chi$-bounded
item.description: arXiv:2512.21800v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The chromatic number $\chi$ of a graph is bounded from below by its clique number $\omega,$ but the gap between these two values can be arbitrary large. Perfect graphs are defined by the condition that $\chi=\omega$ for all induced subgraphs. An interesting relaxation are $\chi$-bounded graph classes, where $\chi\leq f(\omega)$ for some suitable function $f.$ It is not always possible to achieve this with a polynomial $f.$ The edge ideal $I_G$ of a graph $G$ is generated by monomials $x_ux_v$ for each edge $uv$ of $G.$ The bi-graded betti numbers $\beta_{i,j}(I)$ are central algebraic geometric invariants. We study the graph classes where for some fixed $i,j$ that syzygy vanishes, that is, $\beta_{i,j}(I_G)=0.$ We prove that $\chi\leq f(\omega),$ where $f$ is a polynomial of degree $2j-2i-4.$ For the elementary special case $\beta_{i,2i+2}(I_G)=0,$ this amounts to that $(i+1)K_2$--free graphs are ${\omega-1+2i \choose 2i}$--colorable, improving on an old combinatorial result by Wagon. We also show that triangle-free graphs with $\beta_{i,j}(I_G)=0$ are $(j-1)$--colorable. Complexity wise, we show that these colorings can be derived in time $O(n^3)$ for graphs on $n$ vertices. Moreover, we show that for almost all graphs with parabolic $i,j,$ there are better bounds on $\chi.$
item.dc:creator: Alexander Engstr\"om

item.title: Components of the nested Hilbert scheme of few points
item.description: arXiv:2601.16765v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the existence and the schematic structure of elementary components of the nested Hilbert scheme on a smooth quasi-projective variety. More precisely, we establish a new lower bound for the existence of non-smoothable nestings of fat points on a smooth $n$-fold, for $n\geqslant 4$. Moreover, we develop a systematic method for building generically non-reduced elementary components. We also investigate the irreducibility of the Hilbert scheme of points on a singular hypersurface of $\mathbb A^3$. Explicitly, we show that the Hilbert scheme of points on a hypersurface of $\mathbb{A}^3$ having a singularity of multiplicity at least 5 admits elementary components.
item.dc:creator: Michele Graffeo, Paolo Lella
